764.label: Start with the prize winners
764.summary: Six award-winning works. One big question: what makes us human?
764.background: This is the compact centre of the festival’s theme exhibition, bringing together Prix Ars Electronica and S+T+ARTS Prize winners. The Prix recognises media art; S+T+ARTS connects artistic practice with scientific and technological innovation. Look for Hito Steyerl’s Mechanical Kurds and Shin Hanagata’s CHIMERIA: two very different ways of questioning what sits behind apparently autonomous technology.
764.tip: Allow about 90 minutes. Pair it with the Campus Exhibition across Hauptplatz, then cross the bridge to the Ars Electronica Center.
764.admission: Festivalpass+, Festivalpass, Day Pass or partner venue ticket.

769.label: Your first stop
769.summary: Follow media art into churches, gardens and unexpected spaces in central Linz.
769.background: Negotiating the Real examines how institutions, shared beliefs and perception give something the status of truth. This is a self-paced exhibition across eight locations, starting and ending at OK Platz. Its unusual settings are part of the experience: the same artwork can feel very different in a school, a church or a hospital environment.
769.tip: Pick up your badge at OK Platz first. Budget 2–3 hours for a selection; seeing all 39 projects will take longer. A paid guided tour is a separate booking.
769.admission: Festivalpass+, Festivalpass, Day Pass or €14 Festival Walk ticket.

774.label: For a different perspective
774.summary: Art, science and encounters with life beyond the human viewpoint.
774.background: Set in the Ursulinenhof attics, this exhibition grows out of the Studiotopia artist–scientist residency programme. The focus shifts from human identity to coexistence with other organisms and environments. Read the artworks as attempts to extend perception: what changes when fungi, landscapes or ecological relationships become active participants?
774.tip: Combine this with the Festival Walk; it is in the same district. Ask the infodesk about step-free access to specific attic spaces.
774.admission: Festivalpass+, Festivalpass, Day Pass or Festival Walk ticket.

779.label: Hands-on & free
779.summary: Meet the playful side of research at the JKU medical campus.
779.background: The Linz Institute of Technology brings researchers and artists into shared experiments. The exhibition is part of JKU’s Art & Science programme, which makes scientific questions accessible through artistic encounters. It is a useful counterpoint to the more contemplative museum exhibitions, especially if you want to talk to project teams.
779.tip: An easy first hub from your hotel. Add create your world and a medSPACE session while you are here; individual tours can require registration.

789.label: International perspectives
789.summary: Sixteen partner organisations explore our changing relationship with technology.
789.background: The Features programme connects Ars Electronica’s international network of cultural and research institutions. Its perspectives range from translation and the body to the labour concealed inside automated systems. Use it as a collection of different positions on the festival’s theme, rather than expecting one unified argument.
789.tip: Francisco Carolinum also lies along the Festival Walk, so fold this stop into your OK Quarter day.
789.admission: Check the official event page for the relevant exhibition or museum admission.

794.label: Meet your possible futures
794.summary: Explore how humans and increasingly autonomous systems might live together.
794.background: Hello Worlds! emerges from Future Humanity, a research collaboration between the Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota’s Advanced R&D and Engineering Company. It looks at AI as something that acts in physical environments as well as on screens. The prototypes open questions about relationships, agency and coexistence rather than presenting a single prediction.
794.tip: Visit during the day for time with the works. The separately registered Saturday Futurelab Night is currently fully booked; do not rely on being able to return for that event.
794.admission: Festivalpass+, Festivalpass, Day Pass or Ars Electronica Center ticket. Guided tours require separate booking; the Hello Worlds! mini-tour supplement is €3.

784.label: Discover the next generation
784.summary: An international snapshot of emerging art, research and creative technology.
784.background: The Campus Exhibition brings together 45 universities and more than 80 works. It makes the university a place where disagreement and experimentation can remain open. The projects span several University of Arts buildings and MED CAMPUS, so the map pin is an anchor, not the whole exhibition.
784.tip: Start at Hauptplatz 6/8 and ask the Campus Welcome Desk what is interactive today. Leave room for discoveries instead of trying to see every work.
784.admission: Free admission at the University of Arts Campus Exhibition, including Hauptplatz 6/8, and at MED CAMPUS.

239.label: Fully booked · check updates
239.summary: Three decades of Futurelab, celebrated through demos, performances and encounters.
239.background: For its 30th anniversary, Futurelab Night spreads across several floors of the Ars Electronica Center. The evening also celebrates Hello Worlds! and gives visitors a chance to encounter the people and processes behind the research. Expect to move between interventions and prototypes rather than sit through one continuous stage programme.
239.tip: Saturday 20:00–23:00. Only plan to attend if you already have a confirmed registration. Entry instructions are emailed to registered guests 24 hours before the event. Choose the free Klangwolke instead if you have no place.
239.admission: A festival pass, Day Pass or Ars Electronica Center ticket plus registration is required. The official event page currently says fully booked and registration closed.

100.label: Friday night anchor
100.summary: Philip Glass, immersive sound and kinetic music across three concert halls.
100.background: Polaris pairs pianist Maki Namekawa with Cori O’Lan’s visuals in interpretations of Philip Glass. Brigitta Muntendorf’s ORBIT uses spatial audio to confront war and oppression; Daniel Haas’s PULS explores human–machine relationships. Performances repeat through the evening, letting you build your own sequence between Posthof’s halls.
100.tip: Friday 18:30–22:30; aim to arrive at 18:00. Take bus 27 to Posthofstraße or 46 to Hafenportal, then walk. Eat beforehand and allow time for the journey.
100.admission: Festivalpass+ only (€230 full price). No standalone concert ticket; no additional concert registration required with this pass.

243.label: If you still have energy
243.summary: Keep Friday going with audiovisual performances, live acts and DJ sets.
243.background: Ars Electronica Nightline brings the festival into club territory at Posthof. The programme treats sound, physical presence and political expression as part of the same conversation. It follows Big Concert Night in the same venue, making it an optional late extension rather than another cross-city journey.
243.tip: Friday 23:00 to Saturday 04:00. Entry is 18+. Look up your late return before committing; daytime buses will not run all night.
243.admission: €16 full / €11 reduced; included with Festivalpass+, Festivalpass or Friday Day Pass.

487.label: For the big questions
487.summary: What would it mean to build AI with people affected by crisis?
487.background: Developed with CARE Austria, this conference focuses on humanitarian, social and environmental uses of AI. A useful question to carry into the sessions is who defines the problem and who participates in designing the response. This adds social context to the AI artworks and prototypes elsewhere in the festival.
487.tip: Friday 10:00–14:00 in the Ursulinensaal. Treat this as an alternative to a full morning of exhibitions; arrive for the sessions you most want to hear.
487.admission: Festivalpass+, Festivalpass, Day Pass or conference day ticket.

510.label: Sunday’s deeper dive
510.summary: Water as a resource, a witness and a political relationship.
510.background: This conference considers the legal, geopolitical and imaginative systems through which people relate to water. Rather than viewing environmental questions only as engineering problems, it asks how commerce, conflict and cultural perspectives shape them. It pairs well with the ecological themes in Negotiating Beyond Humanity.
510.tip: Sunday 11:00–15:00. Check your departure time before adding the whole programme; the detailed listing is titled Negotiating with Water.
510.admission: Festivalpass+, Festivalpass, Day Pass or conference day ticket.

547.label: Saturday night · free
547.summary: A large outdoor audiovisual spectacle beside the Danube.
547.background: The Danube becomes a stage for a musical story carried by a ship. The Bruckner Orchester Linz, conducted by Markus Poschner, joins baritone Rafael Fingerlos and the St. Florianer Sängerknaben. Composers Flora Marlene Geißelbrecht and Arthur Fussy connect historical and contemporary sound, from Bruckner to the Beatles, in an outdoor reflection on the city and its future.
547.tip: Saturday 20:30–21:30 in Donaupark. Arrive early for a riverside spot and allow time for crowds. This is our suggested alternative to the fully booked Futurelab Night.
547.admission: Free admission, according to the official event page.

622.label: For adventurous listeners
622.summary: Spatial sound, electroacoustic experiments and audiovisual work at Bruckner University.
622.background: Sonic Saturday brings artists, researchers and curious listeners together around experimental sound. The umbrella programme includes installations and sessions across multiple days, even though its title says Saturday. The university is outside the compact central festival route, so make the trip for a particular session or a longer block.
622.tip: Use the individual session times in the planner, not the name, to choose your day. Check the official page before travelling; overview and session dates can differ.
622.admission: Check the official session page for access requirements.

270.label: A curator’s perspective
270.summary: See the Lentos exhibition through Emiko Ogawa’s curatorial perspective.
270.background: An expert tour can reveal the decisions behind an exhibition: why these works sit together and how they relate to the theme. This is an English-language opportunity to spend more focused time with the award-winning works at Lentos, and a good alternative to an independent visit.
270.tip: Sunday 10:00–11:30. Book the tour slot separately and arrive 15 minutes early. Pair with lunch, keeping the airport transfer in mind.
270.admission: WE GUIDE YOU booking required; €6 surcharge with an eligible festival ticket, otherwise €16 full price.

453.label: Meet the co-curator
453.summary: An English-language route into more-than-human art with Masha Zolotova.
453.background: Co-curator Masha Zolotova guides this exploration of Negotiating Beyond Humanity. It offers context for works that consider care, perception and agency beyond people alone. Choose it if you enjoy discussing the ideas behind an exhibition rather than navigating the works entirely on your own.
453.tip: Sunday 11:30–13:00. Book ahead and use the exact WE GUIDE YOU meeting point. This overlaps the water conference.
453.admission: Separate guided-tour booking; €6 supplement with an eligible pass, otherwise €16 full price.

1179.label: Look beneath the AI
1179.summary: Hito Steyerl follows the human labour hidden behind automated images.
1179.background: Mechanical Kurds connects contemporary digital microwork with the historical chess-playing Mechanical Turk, which concealed a human operator. Steyerl combines documentary investigation and speculative elements to make the labour and geography behind AI visible. Ask what has to disappear from view for a system to look autonomous.
1179.tip: Find it inside the Lentos theme exhibition. Keep time for the moving-image work rather than treating it as a quick walk-by.
1179.admission: Part of the Lentos exhibition; use its admission conditions.

1249.label: Rethink your body
1249.summary: Shin Hanagata experiments with moving the viewpoint to remake bodily perception.
1249.background: CHIMERIA combines cameras and head-mounted displays to rearrange how a body is perceived. The project involved volunteers adapting to altered viewpoints in a shared living environment. It makes an abstract question physical: how much of your sense of self depends on where your eyes appear to be?
1249.tip: Part of the Lentos exhibition. Check with staff which aspects can be experienced directly and which are documentation.
1249.admission: Part of the Lentos exhibition; use its admission conditions.
